static_traits.name: Chen Beili
static_traits.family_status: Lives with family; described as 'family members are tall'
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy or counseling received in the past; no similar academic problems have emerged before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, capable of self-Reflection; often using labeling self-evaluations like 'I am a dumb Student'; calm tone but negative-leaning self-evaluation

basic_info.main_problem: I have long struggled to get good grades at school, so I often label myself a 'dumb Student.'
basic_info.core_demands: These negative thoughts keep affecting my self-esteem and overall well-being; I just do not want to keep feeling bad about myself.
growth_experiences: After poor exam performance last semester, started labeling myself a 'dumb Student' when receiving low scores or facing setbacks in Learning; this gradually Reinforced a negative self-concept, causing Decreased self-esteem, weakened Learning motivation, and affecting interest in activities like dance.

Long-term pressure from family academic achievement: believing I need to reach the family's academic level to prove myself, thus feeling tense and ashamed in Interpersonal relationships, choosing not to discuss academic struggles with friends.

core_beliefs: I am a dumb Student / I am very stupid
I am not suited for Learning (insufficient ability)

special_situations.event: Failing exams or receiving low grades last semester
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If exam scores are poor, it proves I am dumb and not suited for Learning
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Studies doubly hard and seeks help from teachers to prove oneself and improve grades
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am too dumb; I simply cannot learn this material

special_situations.event: When encountering difficult problems and getting stuck in math learning
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot grasp or immediately learn something at once, it means I lack ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets stricter study goals, practices repeatedly, tries to study harder
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited for math / I am doomed to never learn well

special_situations.event: Thinking about or facing family members' higher academic achievements and expectations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach the family's academic level, I will disappoint them, showing I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Studies harder to meet family standards, while avoiding discussing studies with friends to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as my family, I let them down

special_situations.event: When interacting with friends involves academic topics, or thinking about telling friends about academic difficulties
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I expose my academic struggles, others will look down on me and will not understand me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeps silent, avoids discussing academic problems with friends
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am stupid

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized by family and others, to be seen as a 'capable Student'
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being judged stupid, humiliated, or Being rejected
defense_goal: Maintaining fragile self-esteem by avoiding exposing failure and doubling efforts
Preemptive self-deprecation to reduce the harm from harsher external evaluation

object_relations.self_representation: A student who is not good enough and prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh evaluators who use grades as the only standard (family/significant others)

object_relations.self_representation: A failure too ashamed to speak of it
object_relations.object_representation: Peers who will not understand and may look down on me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about or thinking about his exam failures and low scores
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others (including the counselor) may judge me by grades just like my family, thinking I am stupid
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cautious tone, tending to say 'They will not understand me', avoiding going into detail, moderately blurring the failure situation.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When noticing family members' high academic achievements or hearing the thought 'I must reach the family's standards' rise within
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes external rules are absolute, that one must obey them and define value by grades
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: use 'should/must' sentence patterns for self-Demands, emphasizing meeting standards over emotional needs.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When needing to ask friends for help or talk about academic difficulties
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that exposing difficulties will bring humiliation and being looked down upon
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Declining communication with the excuse of 'I am too embarrassed, do not want to trouble others', using Interpretive language to downplay the need for help.

manifestations: Feeling one must meet the family's academic standards
Making grades the condition of self-worth
Having friends yet unwilling to discuss academic struggles
Choosing Silence for fear of not being understood
Loses motivation and enjoyment for activities once liked, such as dancing

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats family members' academic standards as absolute requirements for oneself
use'I must/should reach my family's level'
When grades are low, directly links self-worth to grades

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assume friends will look down on me, not understand my academic struggles
Pre-judging others' negative views in social situations

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Clearly need others' support yet choose Silence and self-Repression
not discuss studies with friends, endure pressure alone

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently label myself as 'stupid Student', excessively harsh self-criticism and Self-denial
Cautious when communicating, avoid exposing inadequacy

exception_events.target_problem: When encountering difficulties in academic exams or Learning, the client usually labels themselves as 'stupid Student', Low mood and reduced engagement in Learning.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last year scored high on an essay task, unlike the Self-denial during past low scores, that experience brought a sense of competence and pride.
exception_events.reason: Clue: this task type better fits their own strengths, they were more engaged at the time and made full preparations; the positive feedback provided evidence of ability, so this time a deviation point of a sense of competence and raised self-esteem appeared.

positive_force: There is evidence of ability (high essay score last year)
Willing to seek teachers' help and try new learning methods
Willing to openly participate in counseling and conduct behavioral experiments
Has communicative friend resources(though temporarily not yet used)
negative_force: Comparison with family leads to dependence on external approval
Ashamed to seek help and Social avoidance
Black-and-white thinking during Learning setbacks causes Decreased motivation

target_behavior.behavior: When receiving low scores or encountering Learning difficulties, label myself as 'stupid Student', accompanied by Low mood and Learning avoidance
antecedent: Thinking of the family's high academic achievements and expectations
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralization and a black-and-white view of ability, and Introjection of the family's academic standards as judgments of self-worth
target_behavior.function: Temporarily escape failure and shame, reduce Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: LearningDecreased motivation, grades further affected, Interpersonal tension, reduced participation in activities of interest

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids discussing academic difficulties with friends or seeking support
antecedent: When interacting with friends involves academic topics
Feeling ashamed after receiving low scores
target_behavior.core_reason: Worry about being looked down on (mind-reading style assumption), fear that exposing inadequacy will invite humiliation
target_behavior.function: Avoid negative evaluation and interpersonal discomfort
target_behavior.consequence: Social support not yet utilized, Loneliness intensified, Further decline in self-esteem
